The sun has long since retired, leaving behind a canvas of stars that stretch out as far as the eye can see, each one a silent sentinel of the cosmos, whispering tales of time and space in a language only the universe understands. The moon, a silver crescent, hangs low in the sky, casting its ethereal glow upon the earth below, illuminating the path for those who dare to tread upon it.

I am seated on the weathered bench at the edge of the cliff, the one that has borne witness to countless sunsets and sunrises, to the ebb and flow of the tides, and to the silent conversations of those who have come before me.
